title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 442
paragraphs: Some say that the Samians sent away by Polycrates never reached Egypt, but when they arrived on their voyage at Carpathos, they took counsel among themselves and resolved not to sail any farther. Others say they reached Egypt and were kept under guard there, but made their escape from there. Then, as they were sailing toward Samos, Polycrates encountered them with ships and engaged them in battle. Those who were returning home had the upper hand and landed on the island; but having fought a land-battle on the island, they were worsted, and so sailed to Lacedemon. Some, however, say that those from Egypt defeated Polycrates in the battle; but in my opinion this is not correct, for there would have been no need for them to call for help from the Lacedemonians if they had been able by themselves to bring Polycrates to terms. Nor, moreover, is it reasonable to suppose that, since he had foreign mercenaries and native archers in great numbers, he was defeated by the returning Samians, who were but few. Then Polycrates gathered together the children and wives of his subjects and confined them in the ship-sheds, keeping them ready so that, if his subjects should desert to the side of the returning exiles, he might burn them along with the sheds.
